what: Raw MCP JSON-RPC exchange with the ingredient database server over stdio
captured_with: w9_wire_capture.py - hand-written JSON lines on stdin/stdout, no SDK client, no model
sequence: initialize -> notifications/initialized -> tools/list -> tools/call (+ a failing tools/call)
where_the_model_call_happens: The model is called only by the host (w9_agent.py -> call_llm), BETWEEN tools/list and tools/call, where it reads the tool schemas and chooses the call; nothing in this exchange touches a model, and the server never does.

annotations.jsonrpc: Always the literal '2.0': every MCP message is a JSON-RPC 2.0 message.
annotations.id: 1 = a REQUEST that demands a reply; the reply must echo this same id.
annotations.method: 'initialize' is always first: the handshake that fixes version and capabilities.
annotations.params: What the client offers the server.
annotations.params.protocolVersion: The newest MCP revision this client speaks (2026-07-28).
annotations.params.capabilities: Empty: this bare client offers no sampling/roots/elicitation back to the server.
annotations.params.clientInfo: Self-reported name/version of the client - informational, not authentication.

annotations.id: 1 - matches the request, which is how the client pairs replies with requests.
annotations.result: Success (a failure would carry an 'error' member instead of 'result').
annotations.result.capabilities: What this server offers: tools, resources and prompts. listChanged:false means it will never push a 'my tool list changed' notification.
annotations.result.protocolVersion: 2025-11-25, NOT the 2026-07-28 the client asked for: the server negotiated down to the newest revision its handshake supports. The client must accept this version or disconnect.
annotations.result.serverInfo: Self-reported identity 'ingredient-db', version empty. Unverified - it tells you what the server CLAIMS to be, which is why the risk note matters.

annotations.method: 'notifications/initialized': the client confirms the handshake is done.
annotations.(no id): No 'id' field = a NOTIFICATION: fire-and-forget, the server sends no reply. That is why no server line follows this one.

annotations.id: 2 - a new request, so a new id.
annotations.method: 'tools/list': DISCOVERY. The agent learns its tools from this reply rather than from anything hard-coded - the reason server two needed no agent change.
annotations.params: Empty object; a cursor would go here to page through a long tool list.

exchange.raw_line:
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"result":{"tools":[{"description":"Look up the allergen flags for ONE ingredient by name, e.g. "urad dal" or
    "Gingelly (sesame) oil". Returns every allergen class (dairy, sesame, nuts,
    coconut, soy, gluten, mustard) as true/false, plus the list it contains.
    Call once per ingredient. If the name is not found, the error lists the
    closest entries - retry with one of them; never assume an unknown
    ingredient is allergen-free. Does not return nutrition.","inputSchema":{"properties":{"ingredient":{"title":"Ingredient","type":"string"}},"required":["ingredient"],"type":"object","title":"lookup_allergensArguments"},"name":"lookup_allergens"},{"description":"Look up approximate nutrition per 100 g for ONE ingredient by name:
    kcal, protein_g, fat_g, carbs_g. Values are reference approximations, not
    lab results. If the ingredient is known but has no nutrition recorded, the
    error says so - do not estimate a figure. Does not return allergens.","inputSchema":{"properties":{"ingredient":{"title":"Ingredient","type":"string"}},"required":["ingredient"],"type":"object","title":"lookup_nutritionArguments"},"name":"lookup_nutrition"}]}}

tools.description:
Look up the allergen flags for ONE ingredient by name, e.g. "urad dal" or
    "Gingelly (sesame) oil". Returns every allergen class (dairy, sesame, nuts,
    coconut, soy, gluten, mustard) as true/false, plus the list it contains.
    Call once per ingredient. If the name is not found, the error lists the
    closest entries - retry with one of them; never assume an unknown
    ingredient is allergen-free. Does not return nutrition.
tools.name: lookup_allergens

tools.description:
Look up approximate nutrition per 100 g for ONE ingredient by name:
    kcal, protein_g, fat_g, carbs_g. Values are reference approximations, not
    lab results. If the ingredient is known but has no nutrition recorded, the
    error says so - do not estimate a figure. Does not return allergens.
tools.name: lookup_nutrition

annotations.result.tools: Two tools. For each: 'name' (what tools/call must use), 'description' (the docstring VERBATIM - this is the text the model reads to decide when to call it, i.e. the docstring is a prompt), and 'inputSchema' (JSON Schema for the arguments). The 'title' keys inside inputSchema are why w9_agent.clean_schema strips them before handing schemas to Gemini.

annotations.method: 'tools/call': EXECUTE one tool. In the real agent the host builds this from the model's chosen function call; here it was typed by hand, proving the protocol itself needs no model.
annotations.params.name: 'lookup_allergens' - the bare server-side name. The agent's model saw it as 'ingredient_db__lookup_allergens'; the host strips the prefix before this call.
annotations.params.arguments: Must satisfy the inputSchema from tools/list.

annotations.result.content: A list of content blocks; here one text block holding the allergen flags as JSON text. This text is what the host feeds back to the model.
annotations.result.isError: false: the lookup succeeded - sesame is true for gingelly oil.

annotations.method: 'tools/call' again, deliberately with an ingredient the database lacks.

exchange.raw_line: {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":4,"result":{"content":[{"text":"Error executing tool lookup_allergens: no ingredient matched 'creme fraiche lite' and nothing is close. The database holds 37 ingredients; check the spelling rather than assuming the ingredient is allergen-free.","type":"text"}],"isError":true}}

content.text: Error executing tool lookup_allergens: no ingredient matched 'creme fraiche lite' and nothing is close. The database holds 37 ingredients; check the spelling rather than assuming the ingredient is allergen-free.

annotations.result: Note: still a JSON-RPC RESULT, not a JSON-RPC 'error'. A failed TOOL is not a failed PROTOCOL - the transport worked perfectly; only the lookup missed.
annotations.result.content: The failure is explained in plain words the model can act on (check the spelling; do not assume allergen-free). The SDK prefixed 'Error executing tool lookup_allergens:' to the server's own message.
annotations.result.isError: true: tells the host this is an error message, not data - so a spelling miss is distinguishable from a dead server (which would be a JSON-RPC error or a broken pipe, never an isError result).
